title: Remove flutter_test_config.dart's FlutterError.onError GoogleFonts filter — TestWidgetsFlutterBinding never lets it run during a test
rule: Test-infra correctness (no direct coding-standards rule ID)
why: The comment above this block claims it suppresses 'residual font not found errors... cosmetic rendering issues, not test logic failures' during test execution. I traced the installed Flutter SDK (3.44.1, matching this repo's `flutter --version`): TestWidgetsFlutterBinding._runTest() (binding.dart:1770) saves whatever handler is currently installed into _oldExceptionHandler, then unconditionally overwrites FlutterError.onError with its own handler that just does `_pendingExceptionDetails = details` — it never calls the previously-installed handler. postTest() (binding.dart:2131-2134) restores _oldExceptionHandler only after the test body has finished. Since _runTest() wraps every individual test()/testWidgets() body, the custom GoogleFonts-substring filter installed in flutter_test_config.dart is captured as 'the old handler' before the first test and is never invoked while any test is actually running — exactly the window in which a font-not-found FlutterError would fire. If such an error does occur during a pump, it is captured into _pendingExceptionDetails and fails the test outright, contradicting the file's own comment about what it does.
recommendation: Delete the dead FlutterError.onError override (lines 17-22), or replace it with a mechanism proven to run mid-test (e.g. wrap only the specific pump inside affected tests, or fix the font-loading gap in finding 'golden_runner.dart never renders real glyphs' so the underlying error stops occurring). Do not rely on a global onError swap in this file for anything that needs to suppress errors during pumpWidget/pumpAndSettle.
acceptance_criteria: A widget test that deliberately throws/renders a FlutterError whose message contains 'GoogleFonts' mid-pump either fails (proving the current filter does nothing) or is demonstrated to pass only via a mechanism that actually executes during _runTest's window.
The doc comment above the handler is removed or corrected to match what the code can actually do.
